title: Post-Payment Audit: QuickFix Auto â€” Ghost Repairs
text: Post-payment forensic audit of QuickFix Auto reveals ghost repairs on 8 of 12 sampled claims. Parts billed as 'replaced OEM' were confirmed to be either never installed or were the original damaged parts painted over. Total billing irregularity exposure estimated at $187,000. Photographic evidence obtained from social media of claimants' vehicles post-repair shows no evidence of bumper replacement or frame straightening â€” both of which were line items on final bills. Parts invoices supplied by QuickFix were traced to a parts vendor with no physical inventory. The vendor's address resolves to a residential mailbox store. QuickFix's owner is also listed as the registered agent for three shell companies that processed 'towing administration fees' totalling $78,400 over the audit period. This pattern is consistent with organized fraud â€” not an isolated incident.

title: Post-Payment Audit: Certified Auto Care — Steering Fees
text: Audit of Certified Auto Care reveals 'towing administration fees' totalling $61,200 paid to Peachtree Towing Admin LLC, a shell with no employees. 48 towed vehicles in 6 months came from one I-285 corridor. Tow referral kickbacks are suspected; the shop shows unusual claim frequency for the region.

title: Post-Payment Audit: Ace Collision — Vendor Chain
text: Parts invoices from West Coast Parts Supply LLC resolve to a residential mailbox store. 31% of sampled invoices billed replacement parts that were never installed. Ghost repairs are confirmed on 9 of 29 sampled claims. Exposure $348,000.

title: Audit Referral: South Houston Medical Billing
text: South Houston Spine & Rehab bills 40+ visits per soft-tissue claim vs a market median of 12. MRI costs average $4,200 vs $1,800 market. Chiropractic mill referrals processed the same claimants within 24 hours of each staged incident. Inflated medical billing is suspected across the ring's 16 members.

title: Audit Report: Shell Company Fee Flows
text: Fee flows through four shell companies — Gulf Coast Logistics, Peachtree Towing Admin, West Coast Parts Supply, and Circle City Admin Services — total $312,000 over 12 months. All four share a registered agent and resolve to mailbox storefronts. Ghost repairs and tow referral kickbacks are funded through these shells.

title: Legal Bulletin: Retainer Solicitation — Region 4
text: Attorney R. Berman signed retainers for 48 I-285 towed-vehicle claimants within 48 hours of each loss. Represented claims settle roughly 25% higher than unrepresented ones. Ambulance chaser activity is a primary enabler of the tow-steering corridor.

title: National Fraud Bulletin: Tow-Referral Kickback Schemes
text: The NICB is tracking a probable nationwide tow-referral kickback scheme. Runners are dispatched to accident scenes and steer claimants to complicit body shops. The scam escalates with added vehicle damage post-tow. Certified Auto Care in Region 4 shows unusual claim frequency â€” 48 towed vehicles in 6 months, all from the same stretch of I-45. Suspected ambulance chaser attorneys are involved in soliciting signed retainers within hours of each incident. The NICB medical fraud task force has traced PIP abuse cases to clinics whose medical director previously had their license suspended. Review of these files shows inflated medical billing â€” MRI costs averaging $4,200 vs the market rate of $1,800. Evidence suggests the shops receive $500â€“$1,200 per vehicle steered, paid as fictitious 'towing administration fees' through shell companies.

title: NICB Advisory: Identity Fraud in Auto Claims
text: The NICB is tracking an increase in synthetic-identity cases in auto claim fraud. Fraudsters combine real SSNs with fictitious names and addresses to obtain policies. CL-203 was flagged for using a synthetic identity â€” the SSN belongs to a deceased individual. Policy was active for only 18 days before the first claim. The SSN was traced to a data breach at a Midwest healthcare provider in 2024. Additional patterns include fake IDs used to pass insurer verification and nonexistent policyholder addresses that resolve to vacant lots. NICB recommends enhanced identity verification at policy issuance, including facial recognition and multi-factor authentication. The synthetic identities appear to be sourced from the same dark-web vendor based on formatting patterns.

title: NICB Advisory: Ghost Repair Networks in Urban Corridors
text: NICB is tracking ghost-repair networks where parts billed as replaced OEM are never installed. Photographic evidence from social media shows no evidence of bumper replacement. Parts invoices trace to vendors with no physical inventory. The ghost repairs pattern is suspected nationwide, with the heaviest concentration on the West Coast.

title: NICB Advisory: Rental Reimbursement Schemes
text: Rental reimbursement inflation is a possible emerging scheme: claimants bill for rental vehicles never rented, using fabricated receipts from a common vendor. Average claim $3,100 vs $1,150 market median. NICB recommends verifying rental vendor invoices directly and flagging repeated vendor ids.

title: NICB Bulletin: Attorney Solicitation Rings
text: Suspected ambulance chaser attorneys solicit signed retainers within hours of incidents, often through runners at tow yards. These attorneys are linked to medical mills and shell-company billing in prior NICB bulletins. Retainer-solicitation is a strongly suspected enabler of staged collision and PIP abuse.

title: SIU Investigation: Staged Rear-Ends in South Houston
text: SIU investigators have confirmed a staged-accident ring operating in South Houston. The ring uses swoop-and-squat techniques on FM-518, targeting commercial auto policies. Phantom vehicle drivers and jump-in passengers inflate injury claims. Three claimants â€” CL-201, CL-202, CL-203 â€” share the phone PH-900 and address ADDR-550, both linked to QuickFix Auto. Post-payment audit confirmed $342,000 in fraudulent payouts across 12 claims. QuickFix Auto was found submitting inflated estimates with ghost repairs â€” parts billed were never installed on vehicles examined by our forensic mechanics. Ring members used synthetic identities and straw policies obtained through an unlicensed agent in Northeast. This is a strongly suspected organized enterprise; the pattern of staged rear-ends with inflated medicals appears to involve CHIROPRACTIC MILL REFERRALS â€” claimants were steered to the same three clinics within 24 hours of each incident.

title: Medical-Mill Investigation: Midwest PIP Abuse Pattern
text: A medical-mill pattern has been detected in claim clusters around Indianapolis. Claimants CL-106 and CL-111 submitted soft-tissue injury claims with identical treatment protocols from the same chiropractic facility. Pre-existing injury conditions were not disclosed at policy inception. MRI and chiropractic mill activity accounts for 75% of claim costs on these files. Both claimants share PH-900 as a contact, a phone number previously flagged in a confirmed fraudulent claim. Excessive treatment billing patterns show 40+ visits per claim â€” far above the median of 12 visits for comparable soft-tissue injuries. Review of prior claims reveals CL-111 was involved in three prior accidents within an 18-month window, all with similar injury claims. The personal injury protection limits were exhausted on all three claims. Possible identity manipulation detected: CL-203 used a synthetic identity with a compromised social security number to obtain a policy 18 days prior to first loss.

title: SIU Alert: Northeast Premium Diversion Ring
text: A premium-diversion ring operating in the Northeast has been identified through straw policy analysis. An unlicensed agent was collecting premiums from 32 small businesses and issuing counterfeit policy documents. CL-201 is linked through a straw policy obtained 14 days before a $92,000 claim. CL-207 also received a policy from the same unlicensed source. The fake agency operated from a virtual office with no physical presence. Premium checks were deposited into a personal account â€” none reached the insurance carrier. The NICB medical fraud task force has confirmed 6 of these policies generated claims totalling $540,000, none of which were validly insured. SIU recommends immediate referral to state DOI and federal mail-fraud prosecution. The agent's brokerage license was revoked in two other states for similar conduct â€” yet continued operating under a different trade name.

title: SIU Report: Jump-In Fraud on I-10 Corridor Claims
text: Claimant CL-105 reported a single-vehicle collision on I-10. Police report documents one occupant. However, the claim file lists three injured passengers â€” two were not mentioned in the officer's narrative. All three 'passengers' retained the same attorney within 48 hours. The attorney has been linked to a medical mill through prior NICB bulletins. Phone records obtained via subpoena show the 'passengers' were not at the accident location at time of loss â€” their cell tower pings place them 22 miles away. Jump-in fraud with phantom passengers is a possible scheme to inflate bodily-injury payouts, especially given that the personal injury protection limits on this policy are $250,000 per person. The attorney's settlement demand cites phantom vehicle damage and exaggerated pain-and-suffering claims unsupported by emergency-room records.

title: SIU Closing Memo: Ring-South-1 Prosecution Referral
text: The South Texas staged-accident ring investigation has been forwarded to the District Attorney for criminal prosecution. 12 claimants, 3 shop operators, and 2 clinic administrators are named. Confirmed evidence includes coordinated rear-end collisions at low-speed intersections, phantom vehicle damage, and inflated chiropractic billing. The ring exploited the swoop-and-squat pattern on commercial auto policies where policy limits were $1M+. QuickFix Auto served as the nexus â€” towing vehicles, producing inflated estimates, and coordinating with the medical mill for claimant processing. Estimated confirmed fraud exposure: $687,000 across all involved carriers. Five defendants have already pleaded guilty to insurance fraud in the third degree. The ring leader is believed to have fled to Mexico; an Interpol Red Notice is pending.

title: SIU Report: Premium Diversion — Policy Leakage Review
text: An unlicensed agent redirected premiums from 32 small businesses into a personal account; none reached the carrier. Straw policies were issued 14 days before losses on multiple claims. The fake agency operated from a virtual office with no physical presence. SIU confirmed 6 of these policies generated claims totalling $540,000, none of which were validly insured. Premium diversion is confirmed as an organized enterprise with synthetic identities involved — the same compromised SSN patterns as NB-002.

title: SIU Report: Tow-Steering Corridor on I-285
text: Runners steer towed vehicles from I-285 accident scenes to Certified Auto Care. Suspected tow-referral kickbacks of $500-$1,200 per vehicle are paid through fictitious towing administration fees. 48 towed vehicles in 6 months all came from the same 4-mile stretch. Ambulance chaser attorneys sign retainers within hours of each incident. This tow steering pattern is suspected to involve at least 12 claimants and an estimated $296,000 in inflated payouts.

title: SIU Investigation: Ghost Repairs in the San Gabriel Valley
text: Ace Collision & Paint submits ghost-repair invoices: parts billed as replaced OEM were never installed — vehicles examined after repair show original parts painted over. Ghost repairs account for an estimated 31% of sampled invoices, roughly $348,000 in exposure. A parts vendor with no physical inventory supplied the invoices. 12 claimants are suspected members of an organized ghost-repair ring.

title: SIU Report: Rental-Receipt Inflation in Maricopa County
text: Claimants submitted rental-car receipts for vehicles never rented. Rental reimbursement claims average $3,100 vs a market median of $1,150. Receipts are fabricated by a single vendor and billed through a shell company. The rental-reimbursement inflation pattern is possible organized fraud involving 10 claimants and estimated exposure of $143,000.

title: SIU Alert: Swoop-and-Squat Cell on FM-635
text: A swoop-and-squat cell stages low-speed collisions on FM-635 in Dallas. Phantom vehicle damage and jump-in passengers inflate bodily-injury demands. 10 claimants are linked to Metro Body DFW, which produces phantom repair estimates. Estimated exposure $187,000. The staged accident pattern mirrors Ring-South-1 with possible links to the same attorney network.

title: SIU Bulletin: Cross-Ring Facilitator Overlap
text: Link analysis confirms facilitator overlap between rings: the South Texas ring, the DFW cell, and the Southeast corridor share attorney networks and shell-company administrators. Phantom vehicle claims, inflated medical billing, and tow referral kickbacks appear together in the worst clusters. Suspected total cross-ring exposure exceeds $1.4 million.

title: SIU Investigation: Chiro-Referral Cell in Indianapolis
text: A chiropractic referral cell steers claimants to Circle City Chiro Clinic within 24 hours of each incident. Pre-existing injury conditions are not disclosed at policy inception. Excessive treatment billing shows 35+ visits per claim vs a median of 12. The medical-mill pattern matches the Midwest ring; 10 claimants, estimated exposure $231,000, paid as fictitious administrative fees through a shell company.
